chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Bix and His Gang and Bix's last session with Hoagy Carmichael
summary: Kline lists the Bix and His Gang sides and the Carmichael session with Bix, Teagarden and others; Morehouse confirms he was there but recalls nothing of the day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: All right, let me see now, and then there was a record made interestingly, before the Goldkett group broke up there was Bix Beiderbecke and his gang which is different from the Loopers, the Chicago Loopers.
And you were on that as well. "At the Jazz Band Ball", "Royal Garden Blues", "Jazz Me Blues".
"Jazz Me Blues." Right. Okay. And then you made a record interestingly, you were I don't know if you
remember this or not, tell me. You were on the last recording session that Bix made.
With Hoagy Carmichael and his orchestra.
And it was "Georgia On My Mind", "Bessie Couldn't Help It" and "One Night in Havana! And you made that record with Bix.
Some others including Jimmy Dorsey, Bud Freeman, Peewee Russell, Joe Venuti, Eddie Lang and you. Do you remember that session at all?
You do. Do you remember anything about the recording session, the day? Do you remember anything about being there?
No, okay. Too much. Were you with Nat Schilkret?
Yeah, that probably comes after - that
was after Goldkette am I right?
